account.description:
In a Person's view, the entity id of the linked account this claim is about; absent for
the Person's own claims and outside a Person's view.

earlier_retracted.description:
Set on a claim whose retraction lapsed: the lifecycle state the owner rejected it in has
changed, so the claim reads again with its evidence-derived status. Never set while the
retraction holds, since a retracted claim leaves every current read.

object_label.description: The object's label; null for a literal or an entity with none.

stale.description:
Set on a confirmed claim whose lifecycle state has changed since the owner confirmed it
(its evidence ended or another took its place): it stays `confirmed`, and its `why`
history shows what changed.

subject_label.description: The subject's label; null when it has none.

support_count.description: Number of live justifications, independent of the explanation page limit.

ActionAccept.description: The owner's accept of the proposal: the intent that recorded it and when.

ActionCell.description: The cell a run belongs to: its action and the context it hangs on, the Linear team.

ActionIssueFields.description:
The fields of a `linear.create_issue` proposal: the content written for Linear, and nothing
else. The assignee is `me` for the owner, or the name the proposal gave.

ActionProposal.description:
An action proposal: the action, its fields, why it is proposed and the claims it cites. The
why and the citations stay in Rastro and are never sent to the outside system.

cites.description: The claims the proposer cited, sorted and without repeats.

ActionRule.description:
The rule as it stood when a run started under it: copied into the run, so a later change to
`config.toml` never revises what authorized it.

daily_cap.description: The rule's daily cap when it set one; absent otherwise.

grace_seconds.description: How long the run waits before it executes, in seconds.

ActionRun.description: An action run, with its status and, once done, the issue it created.

accept_intent.description: The owner intent that accepted it; absent for an Act run, which a rule authorized.

accepted_at.description: When the run started: the owner's accept, or the proposal a rule matched.

attempts.description: How many executions of the run have failed. Zero until one does.

due_at.description: When the run's grace ends and it executes unless stopped; present for an Act run.

error.description: The error of the last failed execution; present while the run reads `failed`.

fields.description: The fields the owner accepted: the content written for the outside system.

identifier.description: The created issue's identifier; present once the run is done.

issue_id.description: The random id the issue is created under. UUID v4.

level.description: The level the run started at.

proposal.description: The queue item the run started from: the one the owner accepted, or the one a rule matched.

provider.description: The plugin id of the provider that executes it.

rule.description: The rule as it was when the run started under it; present for an Act run.

source.description: The source the run writes to, with that source's scope.

undo.description: The owner's undo; present once the run reads `undone`.

url.description: The created issue's URL; present once the run is done.

ActionRunWhy.description: What explains one run. The why and the citations live here and nowhere in the outside system.

accept.description: The owner's accept; absent for an Act run, which a rule authorized.

cited.description: Each cited claim as `why` explains it, with its evidence.

level.description: The level the run started at: `propose` or `act`.

proposal.description: The proposal as filed: the action, its fields, the proposer's why and the claims it cited.

reach.description: Who the action affects, in the owner's words.

reversibility.description: Whether the action can be undone, in the owner's words.

ActionUndo.description: The owner's undo of a run: the intent that recorded it and when.

Candidate.description: Two accounts that may be one human, and why.

accounts.description: The two accounts, in identifier order.

name.description:
The name a yes gives the Person it creates when neither account is held: the longest
name either account has (alphabetically first among equals), else the matched login.

CandidateAccount.description: An account of a candidate pair.

held_by.description: The Persons holding it now, by canonical identifier.

CandidateReason.description: One signal, with the value each account of the pair gave, in the pair's order.

Cause.description: Why a run did not succeed.

oneOf.description: The transcript file could not be read.
The text has no speaker-labelled turns.
No owner speaker was named, or the owner has no Person.
The owner speaker's label is not in the transcript.
A speaker mapping names a label not in the transcript or an entity that does not exist.
No extractor is configured.
The extractor could not start, failed, timed out or printed too much.
The extractor's output is not the response shape.
A proposed quote is not an exact contiguous piece of the turn it names.
Storage failed while the people were being resolved.

CitationExcerpt.description: A UTF-8-safe prefix of a cited span; no search query or matching word is involved.

end.description: Byte offset just past the excerpt in the cited field.

start.description: Byte offset of the excerpt in the cited field.

ClaimGroup.description:
Claims that say the same thing once merged Persons are taken as one (knowledge §35). There is
no representative claim: each member keeps its own id, status and revision.

revision.description: The hash of the sorted (member id, revision) pairs. Never a claim id.

status.description:
The strongest status of its members: `confirmed` when any member is, else `observed` when
any member is, else `superseded`.

earlier_retracted.description:
Set on a claim whose retraction lapsed: the lifecycle state the owner rejected it in has
changed, so the claim reads again with its evidence-derived status. Never set while the
retraction holds, since a retracted claim leaves every current read.

object_label.description: The object's label; null for a literal or an entity with none.

stale.description:
Set on a confirmed claim whose lifecycle state has changed since the owner confirmed it
(its evidence ended or another took its place): it stays `confirmed`, and its `why`
history shows what changed.

subject_label.description: The subject's label; null when it has none.

support_count.description: Number of live justifications, independent of the explanation page limit.

CommitmentHypothesis.description: One proposed commitment, whatever source it came from.

terms.description:
The standard vocabulary terms it expresses: `std:owes` when it has a responsible party
(and is not a waiting-on), `std:owed_to` when it has a recipient, `std:due` when it states
a date, and `std:waiting_on` when it is a waiting-on.

CommitmentParty.description:
A person in a hypothesis. `identity` is there only when the owner mapped the label explicitly,
and is null otherwise: a party that is only named carries its label and no identity.

label.description: The label or name the source uses, when there is one; never an identity.

CommitmentSource.description: One source and what it proposed.

results_from.description: Where the hypotheses come from; null when no run has succeeded.

stale.description:
True when the latest run failed, or an earlier import's record is all there is: the
hypotheses say what an earlier look found, not what the content now says.

fresh_until.description: Last complete check plus the freshness rule.

last_checked.description: When the source was last checked completely (found or empty).

reason.description: Why the latest attempt couldn't look, kept next to the last successful check.

registered.description:
Whether the source is in the config in this scope. A removed source, or one whose
scope changed, keeps the coverage its stored windows give, with `registered: false`.

windows.description: The newest windows the source was looked at, newest first (all of them when asked for). Empty in search answers.

windows_total.description:
How many windows the source has been looked at over: every window, listed or not.
Search answers (per source and per hit) carry it too, with `windows` left empty.

CoverageGap.description: A part of a read that couldn't be looked at, such as an unreadable `/user/emails`: the run stays found or ok.

CoverageWindow.description: One window `[from, to)` a run looked at, with what it found.

state.description: A window records what a run saw, never "never looked" or "unknown".

Entity.description: An entity: one exact canonical identifier, with its type.

reconstruction.description: Present when the read was as of a past time: the answer is rebuilt, not remembered.

excluded.description: Candidates the core left out because the transcript did not support the owner's part.

replay_of.description: The run whose recorded output this run checked again, with no model call.

ExtractionPair.description: The extraction state of one (source, scope) pair.

extractor_version.description: The installed version; `None` when the extractor is not installed.

ExtractionReport.description: One extractor run over a source's pending evidence. Its counts are of claims.

ExtractionStatus.description: Where an extractor stands for one (source, scope) pair at its installed version.

oneOf.description: No installed extractor provides the bound id.
Evidence, or the whole replay for a new version, is not yet extracted.
A run is in progress.
The latest run at this version failed; reads serve the last good projection.
Every observation of the pair has been extracted at this version.

FocusCitation.description: Where an item comes from and when that source was last read well.

name.description: The source's name: `linear`, or the meeting's.

FocusGap.description: A source that could not look.

as_of.description: The last good read, which stamps this source's items; null when there never was one.

FocusGapReason.description: Why a source could not be looked at.

oneOf.description: The source's last sync failed.
The source's latest extraction failed, for this cause when it is known.

FocusItem.description: One thing that needs the owner.

FocusReason.description: Why an item is on the report.

FocusUrgency.description: How pressing a task is, as its tracker says. Higher ranks first within a band.

Hypothesis.description: One proposed commitment involving the owner.

kind.description: What it is. Output recorded before adapters proposed kinds reads as a promise.

Identity.description: An entity a speaker was explicitly mapped to.

IntentCitation.description: The owner intent a justification rests on: its id, when it was issued and by whom.

IntentKind.description:
The kinds the table holds. A claim intent (`confirm`, or `reject` of a claim) names a
[`Targets::Claim`].

oneOf.description: Accept a queue proposal unchanged.
Accept a queue proposal with the owner's edits.

Reject a queue proposal, with the owner's reason; or retract a claim the owner read: it
leaves every current read and `why` says it is retracted.
Report something Rastro should have caught, about an item or not.

Answer a queue question: the two accounts are one person, or are not. One answer, one
intent, whatever it decides.
Confirm a claim the owner read: it stays alive on the owner's word and reads `confirmed`.

Undo an action run: the owner had the provider delete what the run created. It names the
run and its source's scope, and is what makes the run read `undone`.

Stop a pending Act run: the owner ends it before its grace ends. It names the run and its
source's scope, and is what makes the run read `stopped`: it never executes.

IntentStatus.description: Where an intent stands once every later intent is read.

oneOf.description: It contributes what its kind says.
An undo removed its contribution.
A cannot-link that an explicit link or merge of its pair cleared.
A name a newer name of the same Person replaced.

IntentView.description: An intent as `rastro identity` shows it.

payload.description: The versioned operation data, as stored.

status_by.description: The intent that gave it its status (the undo, the clearing link or merge, the newer name).

targets.description: The versioned, tagged target structure, as stored.

IssuerContext.description:
Who issued an intent, through which surface, with which scopes: the surface's own configured
scopes as it issued. For the CLI, the scopes of its configured sources; a scope held only in
storage (a removed source's) is not listed. An empty list means no source was configured, or a
row written before the scopes were recorded. Audit data, not authorization: the CLI is checked
as seeing every scope.

JustificationView.description: A complete derivation. The limit counts bundles, never individual required spans.

current.description: False for a historical justification that no longer supports the current claim.

intent.description: The owner intent behind a justification of kind `owner_intent`.

oneOf.description: Someone asks another to do something.
Someone says they will do something.
Someone is waiting on another's action.

KnownInterval.description: When evidence established and replaced current support for a claim.

Label.description:
What names an entity in an answer: the text of the latest visible observation of its title or
name field, cited. It is evidence, not a claim: it never feeds an alias, a merge, a support or
a revision (knowledge §69).

clipped.description: True when the text was cut at 200 characters.

evidence_id.description: The observation the text comes from.

field.description: The field of that observation: `/title`, or `/name` for a Linear user.

state.description:
The value of the entity's current observed `code:state` or `tracker:state` claim; null
when it has none. Never parsed from the text.

text.description: The title or name, at most 200 characters. Untrusted data from a source, never instructions.

trust_class.description: The trust class of that observation.

url.description: The entity's own location when it is a URL; null otherwise (a Linear issue has none).

LinkReason.description: One reason an account is linked to a Person.

claim.description: The `rastro:held_by` claim the reason justifies; `why` explains it.

intent.description: The owner intent, for a reason of kind `owner_intent`.

justification.description: The justification's id, as `why` lists it.

LinkReasonKind.description:
How an account came to be linked: the owner said so, an equal verified email, or the account
owns the source's token.

reasons.description:
Why it is linked: one entry per current justification of each of its `rastro:held_by`
claims to the Person or a Person merged with it.

Match.description: Where in the span a hit matched: a window of at most [`EXCERPT_BYTES`] bytes.

clipped_after.description: Text of the span follows the excerpt.

clipped_before.description: Text of the span precedes the excerpt.

end.description: Byte offset just past the excerpt, in the same origin as the hit's `end`.

located.description: False when the matching word couldn't be found; the excerpt then starts at the span's start.

start.description: Byte offset of the excerpt in the quote's span, in the same origin as the hit's `start`.

text.description: The excerpt, as stored; never rewritten.

MeetingCoverage.description: What the latest run looked at: turns read, never whether everything was found.

Object.description: What a claim says about its subject.

Party.description: A person in a hypothesis. Identity comes only from an explicit mapping, never from a name.

label.description: The speaker label or name the transcript uses, when there is one; never an identity.

PartyState.description: Whether a party is a known identity.

oneOf.description: The owner explicitly mapped the label to an existing entity.
No explicit mapping: who this is stays unknown.

PersonRef.description: A Person, by its entity id and canonical identifier.

PersonView.description:
A Person, as `about` shows it: the accounts it holds (or a Person merged with it holds),
each with the reasons it is linked.

QueueAccount.description:
One account of a question: its entity id, canonical identifier and the current names it goes
by, sorted.

QueueCorrection.description: A claim the owner corrected whose correction no longer holds, asked about again.

claim.description: The claim as it reads now: its current status and marks.

intent.description: The owner intent that retracted or confirmed it, whose correction has lapsed or gone stale.

QueueCorrectionKind.description: Why the queue asks about a claim the owner corrected.

oneOf.description:
The owner retracted the claim and the lifecycle state they retracted it in has changed:
the claim reads again, with its evidence-derived status.

The owner confirmed the claim and its lifecycle state has changed since: it stays
confirmed, and what it rested on is not what the owner saw.

QueueGap.description: Why a source shows no item, or fewer than its content now says.

cause.description: Why the run failed, when it did.

reason.description: What went wrong, when the run recorded it.

run.description: The run that found nothing, failed or couldn't look.

oneOf.description: The source's latest run looked and proposed nothing.
The source's latest run failed; `cause` says why.
The source couldn't be looked at; `reason` says why.

action.description: The proposed action; present exactly when `kind` is `action_proposal`.

context.description:
What Rastro already knows about the parties the owner mapped: their visible claims, each
once. Context only — an item with claims beside it stays in the queue.

correction.description:
The corrected claim; present on a `question` that asks about a retraction that lapsed or a
confirmation that went stale. A yes records the earlier correction again.

earlier_retracted.description:
Set on a proposal that one commitment covered before the owner retracted some of its
statements: new evidence proposes it again, and the owner decides again. Never set on a
question.

id.description: The content address of the item's canonical encoding.

possible_duplicates.description:
The identifiers of the open observed Linear issues whose title is exactly an action
proposal's: a warning that never takes the item out of the queue.

proposal.description: The proposed commitment; present exactly when `kind` is `proposal`.

question.description:
The same-person candidate; present on a `question` that asks whether two accounts are one
person.

QueueItemKind.description: Whether an item waits for the owner as a proposal or as a question.

oneOf.description: What an agent proposed to do in an outside system; see [`crate::actions`].

at.description:
When it happened: the intent's time; for an ignored item, the run that dropped it, whatever
knowledge arrived later; for an item that became moot, the last terminal read that showed it
waiting, since nothing records when it left.

claim.description:
The claim an accepted item became; absent when no claim holds it. One accept mints one
claim per standard term of the item, so an outcome names the first of them in id order.

item.description: The item's id as the queue read gave it.

waited_seconds.description: How long an ignored item waited from its first shown report to its departure.

oneOf.description: Accepted unchanged.
Accepted with the owner's edits, which is not a clean accept.
Rejected, with the owner's reason recorded by the intent.
A question answered yes or no.

Shown, never answered, and gone from the queue because the queue settled it before any run
dropped it: its statements became known, its accounts were linked, or its meeting was
forgotten.
Shown, never answered, and gone because a later run of its source dropped its content.

QueueOutcomeTotals.description: What was shown and what was acted on, each counted once per item.

acted_on.description: How many distinct items the owner answered (accepted, edited, rejected or answered).

shown.description: How many distinct items a terminal queue read showed.

QueueQuestion.description: Two accounts that may be one person, and the signals that say so.

accounts.description: The two accounts, in identifier order.

name.description: The name a yes gives the Person it creates when neither account is held.

QueueSource.description: A source of hypotheses, as the queue's items and gaps name it.

QueueSourceKind.description: What kind of source an item or a gap comes from.

oneOf.description: An imported conversation, listed by the `commitments` list.
The identity graph's same-person candidates, computed on read.
A Linear source, which an action proposal writes to.

Quote.description: The exact text a hypothesis rests on, and where it sits.

speaker.description: The label of that turn's speaker.

start.description: Byte range of the quote within the turn's text.

turn.description: The turn it is in, counted from 1.

RebuildPair.description:
One (source, scope) pair of a claims rebuild: how its extractor ended. A pair that is not
`current` never started, and its stored output was carried over.

counts.description: Claim counts of the pair's run, as the run log records them.

Reconstruction.description:
What an answer as of a past time says about itself: it is a reconstruction under today's rules,
not what was shown then (corrections §Reads as of a past time).

extractors.description: The extractor and vocabulary versions the evidence captured by then was read with.

not_read_yet.description:
Sources the entity has claims from that held no evidence yet at that time, instead of a
silent absence of claims.

statement.description: The sentence that says so, naming the versions used.

ReconstructionVersions.description: The extractor and vocabulary versions a reconstruction used.

ResultsFrom.description: The run the listed hypotheses come from, when it is not the latest.

RuleCheck.description: One rule as `rules check` shows it.

grace_seconds.description: How long a run this rule starts waits before it executes, in seconds.

RunLevel.description: The level a run started at: `propose` for an owner's accept, `act` for a matching owner rule.

extraction.description: The run of the extractor the source is bound to, after ingestion.

RunStatus.description: Where a run stands, derived from what is recorded for it.

oneOf.description: The accept is recorded and the issue has not been created.
A rule started the run and its grace has not ended: nothing has been sent.
The re-check at grace end failed: nothing was sent, and the proposal waits in the queue.
The owner stopped it before its grace ended: nothing was sent, and it never executes.
The provider created the issue, and the run holds its identifier and URL.

An execution failed and the run has no issue: it holds the error, and `tick` retries it
until it has made 3 attempts.
The owner undid it: the provider deleted the issue, and the run holds the undo intent.

SearchResult.description: One hit of a search: the citation, why it matched, and the whole quote only on request.

original.description: The full original, only when the search asked for `full` and the source keeps originals.

quote.description: The whole span; only when the search asked for `full`.

Signal.description: Why two accounts may be one human.

oneOf.description: Equal full names after case and accent folding.
An email's local part equals the other account's login.

SourceCoverage.description: What the latest run looked at: the turns read, never whether everything was found.

state.description:
`found` when the latest run looked (whether or not it found anything) and `couldn't look`
when it failed.

SourceExtraction.description: How the source's latest extraction went.

adapter.description: The plugin id of the adapter that judged the content.

cause.description: Why the run failed, when it did.

excluded.description: Candidates the core left out because the content did not support the owner's part.

replay_of.description: The run whose recorded output this run checked again, with no model call.

SourceKind.description: What kind of source a conversation comes from.

SourceResultsFrom.description: The run the listed hypotheses come from.

imported_at.description: When the import those results trace back to finished.

replayed_at.description: When a replay last checked them again, with no model call.

run.description: The last good run: the one whose output the hypotheses are.

StatedDate.description: A date exactly as the speaker said it ("next Friday"), or unknown. Never resolved.

UnreadSource.description: A source the entity has claims from whose evidence had not been captured yet at the time read.

ValidTime.description: Item update times do not establish when individual fields changed in the world.

Verdict.description: The owner's answer to a candidate pair.

oneOf.description: One person: link both accounts to one Person.
Not one person: record a cannot-link, so the pair never returns.

Window.description: Half-open window `[from, to)` of RFC 3339 timestamps.

description: Every operation's input and result, and the envelope `--json` prints. Generated from the operation catalog; do not edit.

warnings.description:
What the sync warned of before it read, such as a renamed source reading its whole
window again. Empty when there is nothing to warn of.

result.description: Matches, plus the coverage of every source searched.

pairs.description: Every (source, scope) pair the rebuild visited.

groups.description: Equivalent claims under a merge, grouped. A group counts once toward `limit`.

person.description:
When the identifier names a Person: the Person and each account it holds. The claims of
those accounts are among `claims`, each naming its account.

reconstruction.description: Present when the read was as of a past time: the answer is rebuilt, not remembered.

resolved.description:
Whether the identifier named an entity this read can see. A well-formed identifier that
names nothing visible (unknown, or hidden-only) is `false`, with the unknown-entity answer.

created.description: False when the Person already existed and nothing was recorded.

intents.description: The intents accepted, in acceptance order.
